segments.text: Interviewer: Thanks for joining us to talk about shipping machine learning features.
Founder: Happy to be here; we have learned a lot the hard way.
Interviewer: How do you decide when an ML feature is ready to ship?
Founder: First we run offline evals on a labeled set with clear metrics.
Founder: Those metrics include precision, recall, and calibrated confidence where relevant.
Founder: If offline numbers look good we enable shadow traffic in production.
Founder: Shadow mode compares model outputs without affecting users.
Founder: We log disagreements between the shadow model and the current system.
Founder: Then we roll a small A/B test to measure user impact.
Founder: The A/B gate requires a pre-registered success metric and a stopping rule.
Founder: Label drift and silent quality regressions between offline and live data.
Founder: Also, feature pipelines that look identical in notebooks but diverge in prod.
Founder: We gate launches on both offline eval and A/B confidence intervals.
Interviewer: Any advice for early teams?
Founder: Invest in eval datasets early; demos without numbers are dangerous.
Interviewer: Thanks for walking through the validation ladder.
